frequency_question: How often does the central bank execute at least one policy rate cut within 16 months of completing a terminal rate plateau?
membership_rule: Includes all FOMC easing cycles starting from a plateau following a tightening phase, where a cut of >=25 bps occurs within 16 months of the final hike. Excludes emergency intra-meeting responses unless part of a sustained cycle.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named; believed 5 in total for the modern fiat-targeting era under comparable framework structures.
known_gaps: Excludes the 1940s-1950s peg era due to structural regime differences in monetary policy independence.
skeleton: 5 historical terminal-rate plateaus followed by easing within the designated window out of 5 total comparable historical plateaus.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 historical instances matching the structural precedent.
validity_reason: Central bank reaction functions and institutional mandates evolve slowly across decades, remaining stable over multi-year horizons.
